I can't give you the letter for q3. The quiz is still open for practice, and I don't hand out answers to open quiz items. That holds even though you'll read up on why later. Picking a letter you haven't reasoned out won't show you what you can do from memory. I can help you work it out, though.

Start with what the item says is already true:
- The agent has made the same edit and hit the same failing test 40 times.
- All 40 steps are still in its context, so it has seen every attempt.

Here's a way to test any option, and it works the same on all four. Ask whether the option changes the structure of the program around the model, or only changes what the model sees or is told. Then ask what the program would do differently at step 41 because of that option. The stem asks for a change to the agent program, and it calls the change a safeguard. A safeguard has to work even when the model itself keeps making the same mistake.

Look back at your learning record from the agent loop. Your note says the loop repeats "until the model gives a final answer or a limit is reached". That sentence is relevant here.

Run each option through the test above and tell me in your own words what each one would do at step 41. Then tell me which one you think survives and why. I'll react to your reasoning without giving the answer away. Once you submit quiz 0001 for grading, we can go through q3 and every other item openly.
